page: The Microsoft Azure FX64-32ms_v2 is a compute-optimized, memory-intensive virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 32 virtual CPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It features 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

Memory capacity is exceptionally high relative to CPU allocation, providing 1344.0 GB of total system RAM, which equals 42.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or bundled public IPv4 addresses, relying instead on network-attached storage architectures. Additionally, the instance contains zero GPUs, focusing its physical footprint entirely on high-frequency x86 compute and dense RAM allocation.

Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-core performance, recording 2340.0 in Geekbench and delivering strong throughput in image and text processing. Memory subsystems demonstrate strong uncached bandwidth, registering 239.18 GB/sec in large-block reads and 136.4 GB/sec in writes. PassMark CPU tests achieve 52418.89, with strong results in cryptography and physics simulations. While LLM inference for small and medium models shows strong prompt processing throughput, larger models such as 70B demonstrate low generation throughput due to the lack of hardware accelerators. These performance traits make the FX64-32ms_v2 suited for large-footprint in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), caching servers, and memory-bound batch processing.
